claim: In the Hacker News thread on Tracing the roots of the 8086 instruction set to the Datapoint 2200 minicomputer, a reply five levels deep states that, expressed in PDP-11 terms, the Datapoint 2200 had only three address modes: register, register deferred via HL, and autoincrement via PC (immediate operands).

args.query: Datapoint 2200 address modes HL register deferred

verification.evidence_snippet: In PDP-11 terms, the Datapoint 2200 only had these address modes: - register - register deferred via HL - autoincrement via PC (immediate operands)

search_resistance_prefilter.query: Datapoint 2200 "no registers other than HL and PC" address bus addressing modes

notes: Depth counted from the Algolia nested comment tree for story 37102482 and cross-checked against Firebase parent ids: story -> ... -> 37103112 (d3) -> 37103355 (d4) -> 37104173 (d5). Not in the thread title and not in the linked righto.com article, which never maps the machine onto PDP-11 mode names. CAVEAT, stated plainly: the search tool found no page carrying this three-mode enumeration, but adjacent architectural facts (HL as the only 16-bit memory pointer) do appear on the top-ranked general Datapoint 2200 pages, so a model with strong priors could partially reconstruct it. This is the weakest resistance margin in the set. The query deliberately contains no part of the ground-truth phrase beyond the topic terms.
